headline: Highest risk is medium: CrewAI’s default shared workspace and broad egress can leak or misroute dbt-core data, while prompt-injection and cascading errors remain plausible but not directly evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI reads and writes the host working directory and uses shared memory by default, so attacker-controlled content can reach its agent loop. dbt-core exposes warehouse data through its API surface, but no direct parser bridge is documented; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF CrewAI ingests dbt-generated files or logs as instructions
IF both agents share the same working directory without content provenance checks
mitigations: Separate working directories per agent
Disable automatic instruction parsing from files
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts
Review any dbt outputs before CrewAI consumes them

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI has broad network egress, handles API keys, and reads/writes the host filesystem; dbt-core touches warehouse data. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could expose warehouse data through CrewAI’s outbound calls, but the pairwise leak path is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF dbt artifacts containing warehouse data are placed in CrewAI’s working directory
IF CrewAI forwards those artifacts to model providers or tool integrations
mitigations: Keep dbt outputs out of CrewAI’s workspace
Restrict CrewAI egress to approved endpoints only
Redact warehouse data before handoff
Use separate credentials for each agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while dbt-core is runnable and calls a data warehouse. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so conflict is possible only under shared orchestration and appears limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory or warehouse target
IF the orchestrator does not serialize their writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize warehouse mutations
Use lock files around shared artifacts
Run one agent read-only where possible

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate plans or transformed outputs that dbt-core may consume, and dbt-core acts on warehouse resources. Because no verification step is documented between them, erroneous CrewAI output could cascade into incorrect warehouse actions, though direct automation is not proven.
conditions: IF dbt-core consumes CrewAI-produced SQL, configs, or model text without review
IF CrewAI output is treated as authoritative by the dbt workflow
mitigations: Insert human review before dbt execution
Validate generated SQL against tests
Require schema checks before deployment
Log and diff all CrewAI-to-dbt handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while dbt-core touches warehouse data. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a generic compliance gap exists unless sensitive warehouse data is routed into CrewAI’s broader egress path.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is passed from dbt-core into CrewAI
IF retention or residency policies differ between the warehouse and CrewAI tooling
mitigations: Classify data before handoff
Block regulated data from CrewAI inputs
Align retention settings across tools
Document the data flow for compliance review
